ESPN's Ben Solak breaks down why @AtlantaFalcons aren't getting the consistency we need from Michael Penix Jr.

Penix has always been a dangerous big-play thrower, but the Falcons are desperately trying to elicit more down-to-down accuracy from him, especially on quick-game throws. Penix has an 18.4% off-target rate this season on quick passes, worse than all quarterbacks save for the Giants' Jameis Winston; his QBR of 63.6 on those throws is well below the league average (76.0).

Because Penix is a bit robotic mechanically and doesn't have a particularly fluid build, he struggles to get to quick game throws on time, and those late telegraphed releases can draw defenders to the target. He also generally struggles to throw the ball to his right, which is another mechanical deficiency (remember, Penix is a left-handed passer). He has an off-target rate of 25.3% when throwing to the right since he entered the league relative to 18.8% on throws to his left. 

Penix simply cannot handle pressured dropbacks at a starting level, and has not been able to since entering the league. On the season, he is 22nd in the league in EPA per unpressured dropbacks and 36th (out of 37 QBs) in EPA per pressured dropbacks.

There are too many limits in Penix's game. The injury history creates unreliability and limits how easily the offense can get the ball down the field with him. The mechanical issues create accuracy sprays that limit the efficacy of quick games and make the passing game one-handed. 
There will undoubtedly be more and more splashes as the season goes on -- there always will be with a quarterback of Penix's arm talent. But even if he ends the season hot, the Falcons need to see the forest through the trees and understand that they'll never get the level of consistency they want from the position with a player like Penix under center.
